The brief's framing is backwards: the v303 copy path (Copy-Item -> [IO.File]::Copy) writes through a buffered stream whose default buffer is 80 KiB, larger than the whole file, so the file is written in a single buffered write flushed at close; a stall anywhere between create and close leaves exactly 0 bytes (the observed signature). A file LARGER than the buffer would more likely be left PARTIAL (nonzero bytes). So the file is SMALL enough to be left empty, not large enough; its size does not explain the stall (a 7.6 KB file copies in under a millisecond; the stall is an external hang) - it explains only the empty-vs-partial signature, and it explains it exactly
